comparisons.explanation: NASA's 60 m pixel is 0.361. Neighbouring pixels on that map run from 0.447 to 0.580. NASA's 120 m map is 0.601 at the same point. Ours is 0.602. NASA models an observer on the surface, 18.6 years and its own terrain grid; ours uses an observer 2 m above the ground, six years and the 80 m map.
